opal_domains_reason: Stated first, as the order requires. opalinvest.com is the staff domain: it carries 21 of the 56 PROFILE rows, more than any other, and it is the domain of the two staff addresses that actually appear as actors on tickets. opalinvest.dev is Opal's own tooling domain -- the d7/d8/dt battery identities of earlier rounds all sit on it -- and it is included for completeness even though it carries ZERO PROFILE rows, which is itself consistent with round 7's finding that those six identities have no users row. Both are domains the workspace registers and controls. Every other domain is non-Opal.

reserved_test_domains.which_side: NOT an outsider, and counted SEPARATELY. RFC 2606 reserves .test, .invalid and .example so they can never be registered to any party, so a row on one cannot be an outside company -- it is local tooling. The CTO's question is whether an OUTSIDER is classed internal, and a reserved domain cannot be one. It is counted on its own line so the choice is visible rather than buried in the Opal total.

not_an_opal_domain_despite_the_name: opal.agent is the agent-serial convention this repository's own commits use: a seat serial as the local-part, with opal.agent as the domain part. It is NOT a mail domain and carries no PROFILE row, so it does not enter this count at all. (Written without an at-sign on purpose: the criterion rejects that character outright to keep addresses out, and an illustrative example would trip it -- which it did, on my first pass.)

denominators.note_on_the_projection: This read re-scanned WITH allowedFirmIds projected. An earlier pass of mine reused the round-8 scan, whose projection did NOT include that attribute, and so rendered all 21 firm lists as ABSENT -- an artefact, not a fact. Every firm-list class below comes from the re-scan, and the four distinct classes it finds match round 7's per-row get_item values exactly.

totals.how_the_reserved_row_is_counted: The order requires the two domain counts to SUM to the total, and the reserved class to be counted separately AS WELL -- so the reserved row sits INSIDE the side it was put on and is also reported on its own line. I put it on the OPAL side, so on_an_opal_domain is 20: the 19 rows on opalinvest.com PLUS the 1 on a reserved test domain. on_a_reserved_test_domain = 1 is that same row counted again for visibility, NOT a third exclusive bucket. My first pass made it a third bucket and the criterion caught it: 19 + 1 did not sum to 21.
totals.why_the_opal_side: RFC 2606 reserves .test, .invalid and .example so they can never be registered to any party. A row on one therefore cannot be an outside company, which is what the CTO's question turns on -- whether an OUTSIDER is classed internal. It is local tooling, so it counts as not-an-outsider.

non_opal_rows.what_in_the_form_decides_it: the local-part is a single alphabetic given name with no handle markers -- no hyphen, no service or tooling prefix, no digits -- and it sits on an EXTERNAL COMPANY domain. userType is null and plays no part in the verdict: a plain given name is a person whatever the userType says.
non_opal_rows.firm_list_meaning: ABSENT: _profile_scope returns (None, None), which is 'no scope'. So this caller reads EVERY firm, not one -- there is no firm clamp on it at all.
non_opal_rows.last_ticket_event_date: none -- never appears on any of the 27 tickets, verified against a positive control (a digest that does appear matched 5 fields)

twin_first_choice.why: A role phrase of three hyphenated words ending in 'internal' -- a verification identity, not a person and not a service subject with a live outward path. It has exactly one PROFILE row (the service's own count), status active, and an ABSENT firm list, so it reads every firm and the control ticket is in scope, which is what the order requires of a twin. Preferred over the alternate 686bd73cd5e9, which carries an explicit svc- service prefix and reads as a subject on a live vendor path: presenting that identity in a constructed context is more entangled than presenting a verification handle, even for a read-only GET.

alternate.why_second: equally non-human and equally qualified on the three mechanical conditions, but it is a service subject rather than a verification identity

twin_first_choice.no_person_is_used: Neither candidate is a person. Both local-parts were inspected specifically to rule out a hyphenated HUMAN name being mistaken for a handle: one is a service prefix plus a short token, the other a three-word role phrase. The 17 rows that read as persons are excluded from candidacy entirely.

WHO classed the non-Opal row internal, when, or why is not recoverable from the table: no PROFILE row carries an audit attribute, and updatedAt records the last touch of any kind.

Whether the non-Opal active row SHOULD hold the internal firm id is not this read's question. I report the form, the domain, the firm-list class and the dates; the decision is the CTO's, and the order says a non-zero count comes to it before any pair is put.
The other 33 PROFILE rows (firms other than opal-capital) were not examined by form or by domain: the population this order defines is the ACTIVE INTERNAL one, 21 rows.
